challenges.says: The prefix is asked only when the system could not decide one, so a wrongly guessed prefix (first key only; any non-HKEY_USERS key gives just the hive, and an empty file gets HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\) can never be corrected, although the tradeoff says the person must read and fix it; today a typed prefix is kept and only an empty one is guessed.

Nothing is previewed: the system only reads the file and reports a load failure, then applies, so this is the one-request journey split in two with an added confirming click, not a distinct 'preview then apply'.

Replace-or-add is asked only when something is loaded, but today the clear option is always shown and ticked by default, and the 'remember folder only when workspace cleared' rule then depends on an unstated implied replace when nothing is loaded; the title 'without questions' also overstates it, and the failure outcome (workspace may be emptied or partly filled, view rebuilt anyway) is lost.

'Builds the structures once' changes today's behaviour, where loading a single file builds the structures and reports one failure per file, and the multi-file result list and partial-failure semantics are not backed by any legacy rule.

The undo step has no legacy rule and does not say what is restored (the loaded files only, or also the view and the remembered definitions folder) or how long it stays available, so it cannot be done from these words.

Per-file counts of policies, categories, products and support rules are new and ambiguous against the legacy rule that sub-categories and product versions are part of the contribution; the variant is the list-then-details journey with counts added.
The failure step drops that the remembered folder stays unchanged on failure and the view is rebuilt anyway; only the message is kept.
